title: Coral and the Sigil
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse on the night the stars vanish, smuggler and beast-speaker Gideon Okonkwo is dragged from his careful invisibility into a conspiracy older than the kingdom: a sigil-binder has hollowed out King Aldric and wears his crown, feeding on the wards that once protected the realm. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and shadowed by a fugitive royal cartographer named Sera Voss, Gideon follows the old smuggler roads to the free cities, gathering allies among outlaws, talking beasts, and exiled ward-keepers. To save them all he must reach the capital and unbind the king—but doing so means surrendering the gift he has hidden all his life, and choosing justice outside any law. In the end Gideon shatters the sigil, frees Aldric, and refuses a place at the new court, riding north with the beasts who finally know his name.
about_author: Tamsin Sterling is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before trading her compass for a keyboard. She writes fantasy about people the maps forget, from a cabin she refuses to locate precisely.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Gideon, guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell, hears the mountain beasts screaming as the stars vanish and the border wards die in a wave of silence. His POV establishes his hidden gift and his rule: never be noticed. Emotional beat: dread as the world he navigates by goes dark.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Knew
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: a dying wolf delivers a fragment of memory—a sigil burning into a king's chest—and dies in his arms. He realizes the wards didn't fail; they were eaten. He must decide whether to warn anyone, knowing speaking of the sigil marks him. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Drew Roads That Weren't There
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV: caught forging maps of roads that predate the kingdom, she flees the capital's inquisitors and collides with Gideon's caravan. Each recognizes the other is running from the same silence. Beat: wary alliance born of mutual blackmail potential.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: the usurper's inquisitors seal the passes and interrogate travelers with a bone needle that tastes lies. Gideon hides his gift behind a smuggler's mask while Sera's forged maps nearly hang them both. Beat: terror sharpened into cold competence.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Breathe Uneasy
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: arrival in Merrowgate, a free city of merchant councils and refugee rumor. They learn three more ward-cities have gone silent. Sera reveals her family kept the old ward-maps—and the sigil's true name is written on the oldest one. Beat: hope curdling into scale of the threat.

chapters.title: A Parliament of Strays
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: in the city's underways he meets the Unlisted—outlaws, deserters, and beasts who fled the falling wards—including a cynical mule named Bramble who knows his secret. They need a guide; he needs allies. Beat: first taste of belonging he never allowed himself.

chapters.title: The Price of the Old Roads
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: to reach the first fallen ward-stone they must buy passage from the Ferryman's Guild, whose price is a name. Sera offers a dead sister's; Gideon, furious, offers something worse—his scent, traceable by the inquisitors' hounds. Beat: sacrifice as trust.

chapters.title: Ward-Stone Hollow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: they find the first ward-stone drained to a husk, and around it, beasts turned hollow-eyed and mute. Gideon speaks with a hollowed stag and glimpses the sigil-binder's mind: patient, hungry, wearing a crown. Beat: horror and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Letters from a Hollow King
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: intercepted correspondence shows King Aldric ordering his own ward-keepers executed in his own hand—yet the phrasing loops, the same sentences repeating. Sera proves the king writes under compulsion. Beat: pity for the enemy's puppet.

chapters.title: The Unlisted March
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: the inquisitors raid Merrowgate's underways; the Unlisted scatter and regroup as a ragged column moving through Gideon's smuggler roads. Bramble carries the wounded; Gideon, for the first time, leads openly. Beat: invisibility traded for command.

chapters.title: Ash Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: the usurper burns the Thornfell villages to deny the rebels shelter, including the valley where Gideon learned to speak with beasts. Gideon goes silent with grief; Sera must lead for the first time. Beat: grief as the cost of being known.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: a kind Unlisted scout, Pell, is revealed as the sigil-binder's ear—his family held hostage in the capital. Gideon spares him and turns him double agent. Beat: mercy as strategy, justice beyond the law's simple verdicts.

chapters.title: The Second Stone
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: at the second ward-stone they find the exiled ward-keeper Odessa Vane, half-mad, guarding the stone with traps. She agrees to teach them unbinding—if Gideon will let her study his gift, the very thing he's hidden all his life. Beat: fear of exposure versus need.

chapters.title: Lessons in Unbinding
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: Odessa's brutal training forces Gideon to speak with the hollowed beasts and pull the sigil's threads loose—one beast at a time. Each unbinding costs him a memory. Beat: the slow, terrible price of power used well.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Garden
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, via Pell's intelligence: inside the palace, the sigil-binder—revealed as the court sorcerer Mavros—keeps the hollowed king alive as a battery, tending him like a beloved garden. Sera maps the palace from memory and old charts. Beat: intimacy of evil.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: Mavros, warned by another traitor, springs a trap at the river ford. Odessa dies holding the crossing; Gideon's memories of his mother's face are spent unbinding the attacking hollows. Beat: devastating loss, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: with the passes sealed, Sera finds the road she once forged on paper actually exists—a pre-kingdom tunnel to the capital. The Unlisted march into the dark with hollowed beasts as unwilling guides. Beat: her forged maps become true; identity redeemed.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: beneath the palace they surface into Mavros's throne room mid-audience. The king sits vacant; Mavros greets Gideon by name and offers him a place—the gift, unhidden, honored. Beat: temptation of belonging offered by the villain.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: the climax—Gideon speaks to the thing inside Aldric, spending memory after memory, while Sera and the Unlisted hold Mavros's guards and Pell turns his coat at last. Gideon tears the sigil free, and the stars flicker back. Beat: self-sacrifice triumphant.

chapters.title: The Crown Refuses
chapters.summary: Sera's POV: freed Aldric, weak and horrified, must face a court that obeyed his hollow orders. Sera presents the evidence; the free cities demand a reckoning outside royal law. Mavros, sigilless, is unmade by the wards he starved. Beat: justice rendered by the people, not the throne.

chapters.title: What the King Owes the Unlisted
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV: Aldric offers Gideon a wardenship and a pardon for every smuggler road he ever walked. Gideon declines the court but negotiates a charter: the Unlisted become the realm's ward-keepers, answerable to no crown. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Named by Beasts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, coda: riding north with Bramble and the unbound beasts under returned stars, Gideon realizes the hollowed stag and the mountain wolves now speak his name freely. Some memories are gone, but new ones are being written. Beat: quiet, earned peace and open road.
